summary: The approval-run listing pass is extracted unchanged in eligibility, protection, retirement and deadline semantics while overlapping up to four independent parked-run listings; every approval write stays serial, the first record still settles before fan-out, and every admitted batch settles before return. A new fake-port regression test covers hot-tier throughput, failed listings, the three-run write bound, deterministic approval order and deadline draining.

evidence: ops/hosted-autonomy-approval-pass.ts overlaps up to four independent parked-run listings per batch while serializing every approveRun call and settling the first record before fan-out; ops/hosted-autonomy-delivery-pass.ts delegates its check-approval step to this pass.

tests/host/hosted-autonomy-approval-throughput_test.ts asserts seven listing waves for 25 hot-tier records instead of 25 serial round trips, peak read concurrency four, peak approval concurrency one, deterministic record order and unchanged repair state.
The same regression test keeps cutoff semantics: admitted reads settle before return and no read or approval starts after the deadline, and a failed listing still approves nothing.

No throughput threshold is changed (src/host/throughput-watchdog-thresholds.ts is untouched), so the limit is not raised; the focused maintenance-pass latency change ships with a fake-port regression test as the task requires.
